items.stem:
Read the following extract on family and kinship and answer the questions that follow.
"In a matrilineal system, property passes from mother to daughter. The extended family is seen as typical of India, but the nuclear family has always existed. Matrilineal societies are not necessarily matriarchal."
(i) A family with one set of parents and their children is called a: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'patrilocal family' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Matrilineal systems can generate role conflict for men. (2)
items.answer: (i) nuclear family (ii) A family in which a newly married couple lives with the husband's parents. (iii) A man has responsibilities both to his sister's household and to his wife and children.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) nuclear family (ii) A family in which a newly married couple lives with the husband's parents. (iii) A man has responsibilities both to his sister's household and to his wife and children.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Communalism is about politics, not religion. In India, secularism means that the state respects all religions equally. Communalists may be devout or not, but they believe that religious identity overrides all other identities. In the Western sense, secularism means the separation of church and state."
(i) Explain the term 'linguistic reorganisation', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Communalism is about politics, not religion. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The States Reorganisation Act was passed in 1947." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The redrawing of state boundaries on the basis of language, as under the States Reorganisation Act of 1956. (ii) Communalists use religious identity to mobilise people for political power. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was passed in 1956.
